Dad ____1____ (paint) an old garden chair last Saturday. He chose bright red because he wanted to see it clearly from the kitchen window. I offered to help, but he asked me to begin with a small piece of spare wood.

There were two clean ____2____ (brush) beside the paint. I chose the narrower one and watched Dad dip only the end into the tin. Too much paint would run down the wood instead of staying ____3____ the surface.

Dad showed ____4____ (I) how to move the brush along the same direction. My first attempt left a thick patch. I wanted to cover it at once, but he asked me ____5____ (wait) and see how it looked after drying.

The afternoon became ____6____ (warm) than the morning. We moved into the shade and kept working. Our dog sat beside the door, watching as if he had been invited to judge every stroke. We kept him away from the paint and used materials as directed.

After ____7____ (finish) my practice piece, I helped with one leg of the chair. It was ____8____ easy shape to reach without touching the parts Dad had already painted. We left the chair in a suitable place to dry.

On Sunday, Dad checked it ____9____ (careful) before anyone sat down. The red colour looked cheerful against the grass. Mum brought tea ____10____ us, and we sat in the garden for a while. The dog chose the patch of shade beneath the table rather than the newly painted chair. Perhaps he had his own opinion about the best seat.

My brother ____1____ (make) a paper dragon for the school show last week. Its body was green and its tail was so long that we needed a box to keep it from bending on the way to school.

The dragon had two bright ____2____ (eye). My brother had drawn them carefully, but he forgot to put a name label on the box. Mum asked ____3____ (we) to add one before leaving the house.

At the bus stop, a little girl wanted to know what was inside. My brother lifted the lid ____4____ (slow) and showed her the head. She asked whether it could breathe fire. He said it could only breathe the air ____5____ the box.

The driver smiled when we got on. He asked us ____6____ (keep) the long box clear of the aisle. Mum helped us find a place where it would not block anyone's way. The tail stayed folded until we reached the school.

Our art teacher thought the dragon was even ____7____ (long) than she had expected. She found ____8____ empty table where my brother could lay it out. Other pupils gathered around to look at the scales and paper teeth.

Before ____9____ (put) it on display, he attached his label. The little girl from the bus arrived later with her father and recognised it immediately. She pointed ____10____ the dragon and told him she had already met it that morning. My brother said that made her its first visitor, even though the show had only just opened.

The message in our holiday jar

On the last day of a family holiday, we ____1____ (write) messages to our future selves. Dad found a large jar, and we put the folded pages inside. Nobody expected the jar to change our lives; it was simply a way of saving a few thoughts.

We read the pages ____5____ (careful), taking turns so everyone could hear. The jar ____6____ (keep) on a shelf in Dad's cupboard since we returned from the trip. Its ordinary appearance had made it easy to overlook.

One message thanked Mum ____7____ rescuing a wet sleeping bag. She remembered the event differently: Dad had carried it, while she had found a dry place. We laughed and added a note rather than change the old wording.

Before ____8____ (close) the jar, we wrote new messages. It was ____9____ useful moment to compare our memories without deciding that one page contained the whole holiday. Dad put the jar back on the shelf and asked ____10____ (we) not to forget it for another twenty years.

Two birthday poems

For our grandparents' birthday celebration, my twin cousins ____1____ (prepare) two short poems. Everyone expected them to perform together, but each wanted to read a separate piece. They had the same birthday and many shared interests, yet that did not mean every preference was identical.

One cousin, ____2____ poem described the garden, asked to speak first. The other had written about a train journey. Their mother suggested ____3____ (let) them decide the order themselves rather than turn it into a family vote.

Several ____4____ (relative) offered advice. Some wanted alphabetical order, while others suggested drawing a name from a bowl. The twins listened ____5____ (patient) and then chose to begin with the shorter poem because lunch was almost ready.

The first performance ____6____ (follow) by a brief pause while the reader returned to her seat. Then her brother stood up. He had added a final line ____7____ nobody else had heard during rehearsal. Grandfather laughed before the rest of us understood the reference.

After ____8____ (read), the cousins gave our grandparents the written copies. It was ____9____ unusual present, made from familiar words and particular memories. The poems did not have to match in length or style to belong to the same celebration.

Later, I asked whether they would write together next year. They said they might, but first they wanted to hear what our grandparents remembered from this time. The question led to another conversation. I was glad we had allowed ____10____ (they) to make the performance their own instead of expecting two people to behave like one.

The ticket machine beside the window

The station installed a new ticket machine beside the waiting-room window. Its screen ____1____ (describe) as simple to use, and I expected buying a ticket to take only a moment. Then I noticed an older passenger standing in front of it with a puzzled expression.

He asked me ____2____ (help) find the return-ticket option. I could read the words, but the sunlight reflected from the screen made several ____3____ (button) hard to see. The difficulty was not necessarily his knowledge of the menu.

We moved slightly to one side, ____4____ the reflection was less strong. The option became clearer. I did not touch his payment card or enter any private information. A member of staff came over to provide the assistance he needed.

After ____5____ (watch) the exchange, I bought my own ticket. I read each stage ____6____ (careful), noticing that the first screen and final confirmation did not present the information in exactly the same order.

The passenger thanked the staff member ____7____ her patience. She reported the reflection problem rather than simply tell him to practise more. A screen could have clear wording and still be difficult to use from a particular position at a particular time.

It was ____8____ useful reminder about the difference between a label and an experience. The designers' ____9____ (intend) had been to simplify the task, but that intention did not remove the need to observe actual use. We both caught ____10____ (we) trains. The machine remained by the window, with a practical issue now recorded for the people responsible to examine.
